reproduced_failure.result: FAIL: Undefined Behavior at src/digest/blake2.rs:67 (load64), reached from src/evp/legacy_blake2.rs:262 via blake2b::final_ -> blake2b::compress

provenance_problem: In blake2b::final_ the `blocks` argument is `s.buf.as_ptr()`. That creates a SharedReadOnly tag covering the `buf` field (offsets 0x60..0xe0 of the context allocation).

The same call also passes `s` as `&mut Ctx`. On function entry Miri retags that reference Unique over the whole context (offsets 0x0..0xf0), which pops the SharedReadOnly tag created for `blocks` off the borrow stack.

compress then reads the block through the now-invalidated pointer in load64. Under Stacked Borrows a Unique retag invalidates a sibling SharedReadOnly tag for an overlapping range even when the Unique reference is only read; Tree Borrows permits that read and therefore accepted the same test.

This is a real aliasing defect in the source, not a model artifact: the compressor held a mutable reference to the whole object while reading part of that same object through a separately derived raw pointer.
fix: compress now takes the live state fields separately: h: &mut [u64; 8], t: &mut [u64; 2], f: &[u64; 2], blocks: *const u8, len: usize (BLAKE2b) and the u32 widths for BLAKE2s.

final_/update pass disjoint field borrows: `&mut s.h, &mut s.t, &s.f, s.buf.as_ptr()`. No reference covers Ctx::buf, so the whole-context Unique retag that invalidated the read pointer cannot be formed.

The same restructuring was applied to the BLAKE2s sibling (compress, update, final_). The algorithm, vectors and the initialiser refusal test are unchanged; no unsafe operation was added, removed or weakened.
